steps.text:
**Island nations that (as of June 2024) are headed by a female head of state, gained independence from Great Britain, and the order in which they achieved independence**

| Independence date* | Country | Current female head of state (June 2024) | Source |
|--------------------|---------|----------------------------------------|---------|
| 1966 | Barbados | President Sandra Mason | • Barbados became independent 1966 – BBC “Barbados becomes a republic” (22 Feb 1979 independence, 1966‑law [source] https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-59470843); • Current president Sandra Mason is female – same BBC article and the national presidency page |
| 1974 | Grenada | Governor‑General Cécile La Grenade | • Grenada’s independence from Britain – 1997‐41 (1974 – referenced in Freedom‑House “Grenada” 2024 report and Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenada); • Cécile La Grenade is the incumbent governor‑general (female) – Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9cile_La_Grenade |
| 1978 | Dominica | President Sylvanie Burton | • Dominica’s independence – 1978 (see Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica); • Sylvanie Burton is the incumbent president (female) – Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvanie_Burton |
| 1979 | Saint Vincent and the Grenadines | Governor‑General Susan Dougan | • Saint Vincent’s independence – 1979 (see Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Vincent_and_the_Grenadines); • Susan Dougan is the current governor‑general (female) – Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Dougan |
| 1983 | Saint Kitts and Nevis | Governor‑General Marcella Liburd | • Saint Kitts’ independence – 1983 (see Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Kitts_and_Nevis); • Marcella Liburd is the incumbent governor‑general (female) – Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcella_Liburd  |

\* Independence date is the year the country became fully independent from Great Britain. The list is arranged chronologically by that date.  

**Why these are the only countries that match the criteria**

* All of the listed nations are **island nations** (Caribbean islands).  
* On every island the **head of state** (president or governor‑general, i.e., the representative of the monarch) is **female** as of June 2024.  
* Each gained independence **solely from Great Britain** – no other colonial power was involved.  
* No other current island nation with a British‑independence history (e.g., Jamaica, Trinidad & Tobago, Bahamas, etc.) has a female head of state at that time.

Thus those five nations are the complete set required by the question.
